Every release now appends an immutable continuation_released event inside
the release transaction, the ancestry parser treats a released or
never-launched generation as transparent while a generation with any
execution evidence keeps its publication ancestry, and a fully
unevidenced generation refuses fresh claims by name of the recovery.
kew epic abandon <epic> <node> --reason finalizes an awaiting record with
an immutable continuation_abandoned event through the existing
terminalization transaction, releases the reservation and checkout claim,

body:
Contained runs that route through OpenRouter carried the operator's
long-lived API key into the container environment, with no per-run
spend or time bound and no revocation when the run ended. A host-only
issuer client now requests a bounded key per tracked run from the
OpenRouter management API (spend ceiling from the effective runtime
cap, timeout from the run's configured or overridden timeout plus a
300-second grace, expiry validated as timezone-aware), injects only
that key into the launch environment, keeps the same key across
retries, and revokes it at the terminal state; invalid or exhausted
limits refuse before any HTTP call, replies are validated for the
confirmed bounds and revoked when unconfirmed, HTTP and transport
errors are secret-free, and the management key never reaches a
container. Switchyard stays outside issuance because its upstream
credentials have a separate owner; the env: exposure refusal is kept.
The authentication, sandbox, OpenRouter, entrypoint-contract and
security pages describe the bounds. Sixty-eight regressions fail on
main.
Round 1 of the adversarial review on #1957 found two highs and one
medium. A host readiness probe inherited OPENROUTER_PROVISIONING_KEY
because probe_env stripped publication credentials only; probes now
pass through the same launch filter as dispatch (every issuer
management name removed, only the issued run key present). A reply
without limit_reset or include_byok_in_limit passed bound validation
because both lookups defaulted absence to confirmation; both fields are
now required (null and true) and any other shape refuses and revokes.
Malformed-reply cleanup could place the management secret in a DELETE
URL because the hash grammar accepted credential-shaped strings; a
revocation identity must now be a 64-hex hash that equals no known
credential, otherwise the DELETE is skipped with a fixed diagnostic.
Twenty-three regressions fail on the previous head.
Round 2 of the adversarial review on #1957 found one high and one
medium. The runner discovery probes (version and CLI auth probes, also
run by host admission) spawned their children without the launch filter,
so they inherited OPENROUTER_PROVISIONING_KEY; every discovery child now
receives an environment that passed the shared management-credential
filter. The key lifetime covered one attempt's timeout plus 300 s while
the retry loop granted every attempt a full timeout, so a third attempt
could launch with an expired key; the lifetime now covers the complete
bounded retry schedule (attempts x timeout plus the jittered back-offs
plus the grace), each attempt checks the remaining schedule against the
key expiry immediately before launch and refuses (credential_lifetime_refused)
rather than launching with a key that expires mid-attempt, the container
streamer checks its single wall-clock limit, and the docs pin the
lifetime rule. Thirty-nine regressions fail on the previous head.
Round 3 of the adversarial review on #1957 found one high. The
management-credential filter ran unconditionally in the pinned
launchers, so the detached dispatch sink's own `kew epic _dispatch-node`
children lost OPENROUTER_PROVISIONING_KEY before reaching the issuer and
fell back to the unbounded host key (or failed preflight without one).
The sink now launches through popen_kew_dispatch, a dedicated handoff
that accepts only the `kew epic _dispatch-node` entrypoint, requires the
installed kew console script beside the running interpreter, pins its
digest and revalidates it before spawning, and preserves the provisioning
credential for that child only; every generic launcher, agent, container
and discovery probe still receives the filtered environment. The docs
describe the handoff. Twelve regressions fail on the previous head.

title: ignore body outer whitespace when checking a report is current

body:
kew serve's outcome sweep re-exported every syncable run's report on every
sweep. render_report stamps exported_at=now(), so each re-export rewrote the
file with new bytes, mtime and inode even when nothing about the run changed.
The basic-memory index over the sink then re-embedded ~232 reports (~6,700
chunks) per sweep.
export_run_report now skips the write when the report on disk is current:
same body (ignoring the exported_at line) and the current schema line in the
frontmatter. The body is compared, not the frontmatter, because indexers
re-serialize frontmatter (quoting, an added permalink) but keep the body, and
PyYAML is not a runtime dependency. Any read, decode, fence or comparison
failure falls back to the existing atomic write.
Adversarial review found that the probe read any inode at the report path:
a FIFO blocked read_text and hung the serve sweep, an oversized file was
read without a limit, and a matching symlink or hard link was left in place
where the old unconditional os.replace replaced it. It also accepted any
fenced file with the schema line and a matching body, so truncated,
duplicated, or partly deleted frontmatter survived every sweep.
The probe now requires a regular, single-link file under 64 KiB (lstat, then
O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK open and an fstat re-check on the same inode), reads at
most cap+1 bytes, and requires the frontmatter key set to equal the render's
(permalink is the one allowed indexer addition, each key at most once).
Rejected paths take the existing atomic write. A failed check now logs a
warning instead of defaulting silently.

body:
While the repository is private, ci.yml ran pull-request tests on the
operator's Mac with a secret, so an agent-authored PR's ordinary test
file ran on the control-plane host before a human looked (#2033, audit
F1; owner chose option 2). The self-hosted jobs now run for an agent PR
(the agent-pr label, or a head branch under branches.prefix, since the
label is added after the PR opens) only when it carries ci-approved,
which only a human adds. The host clears ci-approved before every push
that updates an existing agent PR (dispatch republish, continuation,
loop, review remediation, ci-fix, resolve) and pushes nothing if it
cannot. labeled joins the PR types; other label events run nothing.
labels.ci_approved is configurable and kew setup creates it.
Closes #2033
The whole-suite gate found the create-kew wizard's label list missing
ci-approved (kew setup creates it) and test_serial_phase pinning the
test job's old condition. The wizard now creates ci-approved; the pin
evaluates the gate (via a shared tests/support/agent_pr_gate.py) so an
unapproved agent PR never starts the job while human, approved, push and
public runs still run both phases and the coverage floor.
Governed review round 1 on #2061. High: kew's ci_green gate counted
skipped as green, so an unapproved agent PR whose tests never ran
passed a loop gate. Each check name is now decided by its latest run
that actually ran (check-runs?filter=all), a name whose every run was
skipped is awaiting_approval (the loop stops needs_human with "awaiting
ci-approved: tests did not run"), and green needs at least one success.
Medium: the approval was cleared even when nothing was pushed; the
clear is now a before_push hook that runs only once there is a new
head, after the scan and before the push, on all seven paths, and a
failed clear still pushes nothing.
Governed review round 2 on #2061. High: GitHub reports a skipped
required job as success, so the epic driver's mergeStateStatus CLEAN
gate could squash-merge an agent PR whose tests never ran. The
check-run decision moves to kew.ci_checks, shared by the loop gate and
the driver; on CLEAN the driver also reads the head's check runs and
merges only when they ran and passed. Awaiting approval re-polls each
tick without a stored hold (a ci_pending hold would stall-mark a node
that waits on a human); a failure or no success keeps the ci_pending
hold. A failing non-required check, or a repository with no CI, now
blocks a driver merge. Medium: the workflow gate was a no-op for
pull_request_target; only push skips the agent check now, and the gate
suite runs every case under pull_request and pull_request_target.
Governed review round 3 on #2061. High: the awaiting-ci-approved
